beats.headline: The princess throne
beats.text: The audience voted Donut a new seat, and Hedy saw to its installation. On the passenger side it looks like a regular bucket seat until Donut sits in it, when a small, fluffy, rectangular bed appears. It is a real product out in the universe, the Ultimate Diamond Pampered Pet Princess edition: it adjusts like a gyro to keep her safe in an accident, monitors her vitals, offers her relief when she is stressed, feeds her snacks on demand and compliments her fur. It came with a creepy man's voice; Donut insisted on a woman with a Polish accent, and named it Dorota. Its existence pisses off Dr. Metcalf.

beats.headline: Arms out of the seat
beats.text: Near the end of the tunnel Donut starts to recast her shield, and the large skull of some orc-like creature crashes through the front and wraps itself around her face like a facehugger. Before anyone can react, multiple arms appear from the car seat and violently rip it off her. The skull and the creature inside are torn to shreds. Thank you, Dorota, Donut sputters. Then, with Gluteus unconscious at the wheel, Donut struggles to get out of the car seat and it holds her tight, so she rips free with her claws, shredding the belt, and slams her paws on the accelerator.

beats.headline: Over its weight capacity
beats.text: Carl is in the seat with Donut on his shoulder, and Dorota does not see why both of them must sit on it at the same time: they exceed its recommended weight capacity. Its breathtaking princess should sit there alone, it whines. Without her it has no purpose, no reason even to exist, and with the nude human added it is unable to function. Carl says he is not naked. Donut asks Dorota to please stop complaining.

beats.headline: Cut off mid-sentence
beats.text: The audience's upgrade for Dr. Metcalf is cosmetic, a hologram. I don't like the way she's looking at me, says Dorota, tightening the straps around Donut. The hologram becomes a giant floating head, and Dorota promises to protect her princess from the obviously senile... and the voice cuts off. The straps loosen. Dorota is broken, cries Donut. Dr. Metcalf, small again, says she has just initiated Dorota's diagnostics mode: the chair might be defective, and will be out of commission for a few hours.

beats.headline: Still gagged, still useful
beats.text: Moments before the heat, Carl has been turned into a long-haired dachshund, and Donut, ready to go, needs the window down. It is manual, she may not break the glass until the heat starts, and Jamal is too snug to reach. Then Donut's chair, still muted, unhooks herself, an arm appears, grasps the handle and quickly rolls it down. Thank you, Dorota.
